subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: For the remaining repeated file-read failures, should OpenClaw fix the scheduled producer paths, teach `read` to handle directory targets, or add a broader repeated-tool-error circuit breaker?
rationale: Current source proves partial fixes and one still-failing read shape, but the best owner boundary depends on whether maintainers want producer cleanup, tool semantics changes, or runtime loop containment.

options.title: Reproduce and fix the producer narrowly
options.body: Use a live gateway/scheduler repro to identify the cron/heartbeat prompt or producer that asks for `memory-system/CORE.md` or `memory/agent-tasks`, then fix that owner path plus focused tests.

options.title: Change read-tool directory semantics
options.body: Treat directory targets as actionable directory-listing errors or redirect to `ls`, accepting a user-visible tool behavior change that needs compatibility review.

options.title: Route to broader loop containment
options.body: Defer the producer fix and handle this under a general repeated tool-error/circuit-breaker design such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/75923.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and fix the producer narrowly
recommendation.body: Use a live gateway/scheduler repro to identify the cron/heartbeat prompt or producer that asks for `memory-system/CORE.md` or `memory/agent-tasks`, then fix that owner path plus focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is closest to recent cron chronic-failure observability and scheduler recovery work, while the final fix may still need read-tool input from galiniliev.
